title: SLO-hedged revocation with GPU compaction rotation for continuous batching
creator: Priya Raman
description: Problem: Continuous batching holds live micro-slices and KV cache residency in GPU memory. Under mixed-tenancy spikes we observe: 1) allocation failures caused by fragmentation rather than absolute free memory, 2) outsized preemptions of low-latency tenants when aggressive eviction is used, and 3) long tail latency regressions from repeated cold-KV reloads. Goals: design a revocation / preemption flow that (a) respects tenant SLO tiers, (b) minimizes repeated cold-KV thrash, and (c) reduces GPU fragmentation via scheduled compaction windows that safely interleave with live slices. Constraints: must integrate with existing continuous batcher and KV accounting, keep incremental changes to the runtime (< 15% code churn), and remain compatible with Dedicated/Private deployments where some compaction ops are slower due to PCIe-bound NVMe backing stores.
proposal_summary: Introduce a hedged revocation mechanism: when memory pressure exceeds a threshold, issue time-bounded revocation tokens to candidate slices rather than immediate kill. Revocation token = (tenant_id, slice_id, warranty_seconds). Candidates are chosen by a SLO-weighted eviction score that factors recent token throughput, KV hit-rate, and active latency SLO band. Simultaneously schedule short GPU compaction rotations on a per-device ring that pick low-util lanes for defragmentation. Compaction is incremental (page-level coalesce + colleague migration) and runs during micro-idle windows exposed by hedged tokens. If warranty expires, fallback to strict preemption. This reduces fragmentation and gives hot KV a chance to stay resident for short bursts, improving P99 for latency-sensitive tenants.
design_decisions: Use SLO-weighted score rather than strict FIFO so premium tenants get longer warranties
Hedged tokens are optimistic: slices try to finish within warranty; if they cannot, they checkpoint KV references and release non-essential state
Compaction will be best-effort and capped by a per-GPU compaction budget to avoid interfering with throughput
Fallback to immediate revoke only when compaction budget exhausted or hard OOM imminent
metrics_and_slo_targets: P50 latency change <= +5ms for P0 tenants on steady-state
P99 latency decrease >= 10% (vs baseline aggressive-eviction) for P1/P0 tenants under bursty load
KV reload rate reduction >= 30% for hot prefixes during 1-minute bursts
Successful compaction cycles executed >= 80% of scheduled windows under normal load
Fraction of revocations resolved within warranty_seconds >= 70% for premium tenants
tradeoffs: Longer warranties reduce immediate capacity available to admit new requests — mitigated by tight compaction windows and admission backpressure
Compaction requires DMA and temporary bookkeeping which increases CPU overhead slightly (~2-4%)
Implementation complexity increases runtime surface area; this is mitigated by a feature flag and per-cluster rollout
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end canary on Dedicated cluster: enable feature flag + run 30m burst test with mixed SLO tenants and compare against baseline traces
Telemetry: expose warranty token lifecycle (issued/fulfilled/expired), compaction windows started/completed, and per-tenant KV-reload counts
No regression in synthetic throughput test (<= 3% throughput drop) with compaction enabled
Unit and integration tests for token issuance, warranty expiry paths, and compaction budget enforcement

2026-02-20: Design review with runtime and infra — agreed on SLO-weighted formula: score = base_score * (1 - recent_kv_hit_rate) * tenant_slo_multiplier
